cohort: The study included 120 pregnant women, evenly split between term (37-41 weeks) and post-term (>=42 weeks) groups, all undergoing elective caesarean section with spinal anaesthesia.
finding: Post-operative QTc interval and frontal QRS-T angle were significantly higher in post-term pregnant women compared to term pregnant women, suggesting underlying changes in cardiac electrophysiology related to prolonged gestation and potential sub-clinical myocardial stress.
cross-section timing: Measurements were taken post-operatively after caesarean section with spinal anaesthesia.
